title: Crystal lattices & unit cells
examples: What is the difference between a unit cell and a crystal lattice?
How do we calculate the number of atoms in a unit cell?
Can you show me an example of a body-centered cubic structure?

explain.say: Today we explore the basic building blocks of crystals.
A unit cell is the smallest repeating unit in a crystal.
Cubic cells are a specific type of unit cell shape.
We must count the atoms located at the corners of the cube.
Atoms in the center of the faces also contribute to the total count.
In a Face-Centered Cubic cell, we sum these contributions.

faq.q: How many atoms are in a simple cubic unit cell?
faq.a: A simple cubic cell has atoms only at the corners. Each corner atom contributes one eighth to the total count. Therefore, there are one whole atom in the cell.
asks: What is the atom count for simple cubic?
How many atoms are at the corners only?

faq.q: Does the shape of the unit cell affect the atom count?
faq.a: Yes, the arrangement of atoms determines the count. Face-centered and body-centered structures have different numbers of atoms per unit cell.
asks: Why is FCC different from SC?
What determines the number of atoms?

faq.q: What is the difference between a unit cell and a crystal?
faq.a: The unit cell is the mathematical model of the smallest repeating unit. The crystal is the actual solid structure built from these repeating units.
asks: Is the unit cell the whole crystal?
Can you show me the difference?

faq.q: If I find a body-centered cubic cell, how do I count the atoms?
faq.a: For a body-centered cell, you count the 8 corners, which give one whole atom, plus the one atom exactly in the body center, giving a total of two atoms.

faq.q: Do all crystal structures have to be cubic?
faq.a: No, crystal structures can be cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, and so on. Cubic is just one specific, simple shape.
asks: Must the cell be a cube?

facts: The unit cell is the smallest repeating unit that defines a crystal structure.
A cubic cell has three edges meeting at right angles.
In a Face-Centered Cubic (FCC) cell, atoms are located at the corners and the center of each face.
The total number of atoms in an FCC unit cell is four atoms.

quiz.say: How many atoms are present in a Face-Centered Cubic unit cell?
quiz.why: You count eight corners each contributing one eighth, which is one whole atom. Then you count six face centers each contributing one half, which is three whole atoms. One plus three equals four atoms.

wrong.0: This is the number of atoms in a Body-Centered Cubic cell, not FCC.
wrong.1: This only counts the atoms at the corners, forgetting the face centers.
wrong.2: This only counts the atoms located in the center of the six faces.

quiz.say: If a unit cell is simple cubic, how many atoms does it contain?
quiz.why: Only the eight corners contribute atoms, and eight times one eighth equals exactly one whole atom.

wrong.0: This forgets that the corner atoms still exist and contribute to the structure.
wrong.1: This only accounts for the contribution of a single face center, not the whole cell.
wrong.3: This incorrectly counts the atoms at the corners without considering their shared contribution.

quiz.say: A cubic cell is defined by what property of its angles?
quiz.why: A cube must have all its angles measuring ninety degrees, making it a right-angled shape.

wrong.0: This is a property of a triangle, not the angles defining the cell edges.
wrong.1: Acute angles are less than ninety degrees, which is not the case for a cube.
wrong.3: While true for a cube, this describes equilateral shapes, not necessarily the right angles required for a cubic cell.
